sanjay: Quick FYI - noticed a 1.7x p99 regression on 8k seq after flipping kernel selection -> fused-flash attn on canary. Need quick triage.
kevin: which model/variant? commit?
sanjay: model: redwood/open-7b-8k, variant: flash_fused_v2; commit: 5f3a9d2 (runtime kernel-selection change). Bench harness ran on ded-1, gpu A100 80G.
perf-bot: perf/bench/attn: before commit 5f3a9d2: p50 18ms p95 34ms p99 64ms; after: p50 20ms p95 48ms p99 112ms (8k seq, batch size 1-4) :chart_with_upwards_trend:
maria: @sanjay can you paste microbench output? Also did KV cache hit rate drop?
sanjay: KV warm/cold matters. With kv-warm: p99 78ms; kv-cold: 130ms. So cache misses amplify.
olivia: ran microbench with simple loop, logs:
```bash
./bench_attn --model open-7b-8k --kernel fused --seq 8192 --batch 2
# results
p50: 22ms
p95: 50ms
p99: 118ms
```
kevin: interesting — paged-attn variant still has p99 70ms on same machine. looks like fused has worse latency tail for long seq.
eva: hypothesis: fused implementation uses fewer kernel launches but larger workspace and serialization points; combined with our "staggered batching" heuristic it increases contention and kernel setup time. Also KV cache page faults increase memory traffic which hurts fused more.
sanjay: I instrumented kernel selection path: when batch_tokens < 4096 we sometimes pick fused due to lower theoretical FLOPS; but for 8k seq the fused path inflates launch time.
kevin: could be occupancy/warp underutilization on small head sizes. Do we have per-kernel occupancy traces?
olivia: yes, quick nvprof dump (truncated):
```
Kernel: fused_attn_v2, occupancy: 0.35, avg_latency: 1.8ms per call, calls per step: 60
Kernel: paged_attn, occupancy: 0.72, avg_latency: 0.9ms per call, calls per step: 40
```
kevin: that explains tail - more launches and lower occupancy = worse p99.
eva: mitigation idea: change kernel-selection rule: prefer paged when seq_len >= 4096 OR kv_cache_cold OR observed kernel latency variance high. Also tune batching heuristic to avoid staggered small micro-batches for long sequences.
sanjay: I tried forcing kernel=flash_paged on canary -> p99 back to 68ms. So immediate mitigation is to pin paged for sequences > 4k or when KV cold.
kevin: agree. let's add kernel selection rule: if seq_len >= 4096 and (kv_cache_cold || batch_tokens < 4096) -> prefer flash_paged. Also add telemetry flag to measure per-request kernel path.
perf-bot: created perf issue #INF-4321 with the attached microbench logs and nvprof traces.
olivia: quick bisect suggests culprit is runtime change in allocator logic (commit 5f3a9d2) that altered workspace fragmentation and reduced small-kernel occupancy. Bisect summary: good (5f3a8f1) -> bad (5f3a9d2) -> good (5f3aa01 with different allocator tweak).
maria: action items: 1) revert kernel-selection flip on canary (sanjay) 2) add heuristic patch and telemetry (kevin) 3) run stress runs across ded/gcp regions (olivia) 4) add e2e perf test in CI for 8k sequences (eva) 5) longer-term: evaluate fused memory layout improvements (research).
sanjay: I'll revert canary now. rolling back kernel selection flag.
deploy-bot: rollback deployed at 1785239902 by sanjay
kevin: thanks. we'll follow up with proper fix and a regression test. :thumbsup:
